scope: bounded, decide-able GPU feasibility probe; standalone script only, production runner untouched

host.cpu: 12th Gen Intel Core i9-12900H (14 physical / 20 logical)
host.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU, 6144 MiB total
host.note: RTX 3060 (GA106) has 1/64-rate fp64 -> the fp64 GPU lane is ~5.8x slower than the fp32 lane

ported_stages.stage3: BlockwiseProfile.blocks - per-image threshold counting via searchsorted differences (torch.searchsorted, batched, +inf padding of the ragged sorted vectors)
ported_stages.stage4: pooled_ap_auroc_multi - block-level (1000 x n_images) @ (n_images x chunk) GEMMs + cumsum + elementwise, on device
ported_stages.left_on_cpu: np.load deserialise, cv2/gaussian grid rebuild, per-image np.sort, np.unique of the positive scores (+ the small-matrix h2d transfer)

correctness.criterion: max|delta| <= 1e-6 vs the shipped CPU code on the same real unit

searchsorted_selftest.note: +inf padding of ragged sorted vectors reproduces numpy searchsorted exactly

float64.verdict: PASS - exact to fp64 round-off, reproducible bit-for-bit across 4 runs

float32.verdict: FAIL - auroc 1.34e-6 > 1e-6; ap 9.29e-7 passes with only 7% margin

float32_with_float64_accumulator.verdict: PASS - and free: 2.3405 s vs 2.3773 s for the all-fp32 lane

float32.verdict: PASS (grid too small to expose the fp32 loss)

localisation.method: third lane: fp32 compute with only the cross-block accumulators (ap[r] += ..., auroc[r] += ...) widened to fp64
localisation.conclusion: the fp32 loss is fp32 accumulation across the 521 grid blocks, NOT the searchsorted boundaries (integer-exact in both dtypes) and NOT GEMM associativity (every block-level mass is an exact integer <= 4e5 < 2^24)

speed.heavy_case: mpdd_s0_k1 / metal_plate / method B (97 images, 521 blocks); all timings taken back-to-back inside one process while the A08 CPU sweep was running
speed.caveat: the spread is environmental (laptop GPU power state + CPU contention from the concurrent A08 sweep); the CPU and GPU passes are back-to-back in the same process, so the ratios are more robust than the absolutes

resources.cpu_side_note: the probe process peak (924.9 MiB) includes the CPU reference pass and the 6 x 1000 x 4096 fp64 pooling buffers (~197 MiB) that the GPU path moves to VRAM, so the GPU-only path is lighter on host RAM than the CPU path

verdict.usable: float64: YES (<=3.4e-16, contract intact). float32: NO as-is (auroc 1.34e-6 > 1e-6); the same fp32 lane with a float64 cross-block accumulator IS within contract (6.1e-8) and costs nothing
reasoning: remaining CPU work is ~9.6-14.2e3 s single-stream (~2.7-3.9 h); the live N=6 run finishes in ~1.4-2.2 h
a completed GPU port would be ~0.25-0.79 h single-stream (fp64), i.e. faster than the live run, but only after the port exists
the port is not just the two stages: it needs runner integration with --shard/--resume semantics plus a fresh 1e-6 revalidation of the products, which is more than the ~1-2 h the CPU run has left
the port also breaks the bitwise-identical claim (3.3e-16 instead of 0) and must be re-validated, and a single GPU stream cannot be sharded like the CPU workers
threshold_for_a_future_port: do it when the portable CPU wall for one run exceeds ~10 h (e.g. >=3-4x the current grid: more datasets/seeds/shots/replicates/methods), so the port+revalidation amortises
or when free RAM caps N at 3 while the GPU sits idle
preferred lane: float32 compute + float64 cross-block accumulator (65x pool, 37x end-to-end, 6.1e-8 error) - but only after a fresh 1e-6 revalidation
failing that, float64 is the safe lane (exact to 3.4e-16) at 5-11x
